standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a base change of an etale morphism is etale and that a scheme etale over the spectrum of an algebraically closed field is a disjoint union of trivial extensions; the section argument and the lifting conclusion are retained in the counted span.

core_obligations: Locate a fibre with a point: since the U_i cover U, some fibre product sbar x_{ubar, U, phi_i} U_i is nonempty, and one then looks at the displayed cartesian square comparing it with Spec(k) = sbar over U (proof lines 3316-3327).

Show the fibre splits: the projection pr_1 is a base change of an etale morphism, hence etale, and a scheme etale over the spectrum of a field is a disjoint union of finite separable extensions of that field; since k is algebraically closed, all these extensions are trivial, so pr_1 admits a section sigma (proof lines 3328-3336).

Produce the lift: the composite pr_2 composed with sigma is a morphism U_i-point of the geometric point sbar whose composite with phi_i agrees with ubar, i.e. a morphism (U_i, ubar_i) -> (U, ubar) of etale neighbourhoods (proof lines 3336-3337).
proof_roadmap: Pick i with nonempty fibre product of sbar with U_i over U (proof lines 3316-3318).
Use the cartesian square to see that this fibre product is etale over Spec(k) = sbar, hence a disjoint union of finite separable field extensions of k (proof lines 3319-3333).
As k is algebraically closed all those extensions are trivial, so a section sigma exists and pr_2 o sigma is the required morphism of etale neighbourhoods (proof lines 3334-3337).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an etale covering {phi_i : U_i -> U} of an etale neighbourhood (U, ubar) of a geometric point sbar of S, some U_i carries a geometric point ubar_i over sbar making phi_i a morphism of etale neighbourhoods (statement lines 3306-3312). The proof converts surjectivity of the covering into nonemptyness of one fibre product, and then exploits the special shape of a scheme etale over an algebraically closed field: the fibre product is a disjoint union of finite separable extensions of k, which are all trivial because k is algebraically closed, so a section of pr_1 exists and composing it with pr_2 gives the lift (proof lines 3328-3337). The non-formal step is precisely that appeal to triviality of the field extensions, which is what makes the covering-surjectivity statement into a lifting statement for geometric points. The claim is H2.
